verdict.rationale: Statsig documents both data paths the story names: custom ingested events are used for metric calculation and experiment outcomes, and Warehouse Native runs experiment analysis directly in your own data warehouse. Scorecards let you select primary and secondary metrics. However, the evidence never shows how a PM actually defines a metric from a warehouse table, or how transparent those definitions are, so this is partial rather than full. Missing for 10: documented metric-definition workflow for warehouse tables (e.g. SQL or metric sources), evidence that metric definitions are transparent rather than black-box, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a product manager, I can define experiment metrics from my own data — warehouse tables or ingested events — instead of a black-box metric store

citations.quote: Statsig Warehouse Native is an experimentation platform that runs analysis directly in your data warehouse.
Logs one or more custom events for analytics and metric calculation. Events are used to measure experiment outcomes and user behavior.
The Scorecard feature makes this easy by letting you enter your hypothesis and select both primary and secondary metrics.
Statsig then forwards that assignment and event data to your warehouse for analysis.
